chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā and al-Ṣaffār together, from al-ʿUbaydī, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man struck his غلام with a blow and cut part of his tongue, so he could articulate some [letters] and could not articulate some. He said:
"The alphabet is recited to him; whatever he articulates is deducted from the diyah, and whatever he does not articulate, the diyah is imposed for it."

He said: I said, how is that? He said: "According to the reckoning of al-jummal: alif, its diyah is one; bāʾ, its diyah is two; jīm, three; dāl, four; hāʾ, five; wāw, six; zāy, seven; ḥāʾ, eight; ṭāʾ, nine; yāʾ, ten; kāf, twenty; lām, thirty; mīm, forty; nūn, fifty; sīn, sixty; ʿayn, seventy; fāʾ, eighty; ṣād, ninety; qāf, one hundred; rāʾ, two hundred; shīn, three hundred; tāʾ, four hundred; and every letter added after this, beginning from alif b t th, you add for it one hundred dirhams."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What this report contains regarding detailing the diyah according to the letters appears to be from the speech of some of the narrators. Since they heard that he said that this is to be distributed according to the letters of al-jummal, they assumed that it meant according to the well-known numerical reckoning of that, whereas that was not the intent. Rather, the intent was that it be divided across all the letters into equal portions, and that each letter be assigned a share of their total, as al-Sukūnī detailed in his narration and others among the narrators. If the matter were as this narration contains, all the letters together would not complete the diyah in full, because that would not reach the full diyah if we calculated it in dirhams; and if we calculated it in dinars, it would amount to multiple times the diyah. All of that is unsound. Therefore, the practice should be according to the reports that have preceded.

key_terms.أَفْصَحَ: he articulated clearly or pronounced distinctly
key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمِ: dirhams, a monetary unit used in calculation
key_terms.الدَّنَانِيرِ: dinars, another monetary unit referenced in calculation
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation owed for bodily injury
key_terms.الْحُرُوفِ: the letters whose articulation is measured
key_terms.الْمُعْجَمَ: the alphabet recited for testing speech ability
key_terms.حِسَابِ الْجُمَّلِ: the numerical reckoning assigned to Arabic letters
key_terms.لِسَانِهِ: his tongue, the injured organ under discussion

ai.seo_question: How is the diyah for partial loss of speech from an injured tongue calculated in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the assessment of diyah for injury to the tongue based on the letters the injured person can still articulate and those he cannot. The closing statement by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan clarifies that the literal numerical assignment by the letters of al-jummal is not to be relied upon, and that the ruling should instead follow the earlier reports that distribute the compensation proportionally.
